newsitem.title: INDIA: Troops hunt India militants after Sunday massacre.
newsitem.headline: Troops hunt India militants after Sunday massacre.

text.p: Soldiers with shoot-on-sight orders combed the northeast Indian state of Tripura on Monday after at least 32 people died in ethnic violence over the weekend.
State authorities said 27 Bengali settlers were killed when separatist tribesmen rampaged through three remote villages, setting fire to houses and shooting their inhabitants early on Sunday.
Three separatists died in the clashes, police said, and two others were shot dead by security forces enforcing an indefinite curfew in the remote Khowai area bordering Bangladesh.
The government said the situation was calm but tense on Monday.

"The situation is under control and the government will take adequate measures to contain the violence. The government will take firm action against all law breakers," Tripura Interior Minister Samar Chowdhury told reporters.
The state's communist-led government came under attack from the opposition Congress party for the sharp surge in attacks over the past eight days by the separatist All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF).
Local news agencies said Congress was pushing for the imposition of direct rule from New Delhi to stem the violence.

"The Left Front government has totally failed to curb militancy and restore normalcy," the United News of India quoted state Congress president Samir Ranjan Burman as saying. "The government should resign immediately."

The Congress party shores up Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front alliance in the federal parliament. The Communist Party of India-Marxist, which heads a coalition governing Tripura and is part of the Left Front grouping, is a member of the United Front.
Army reinforcements and paramilitary battalions rushed to Tripura were granted sweeping shoot-at-sight orders after the Sunday massacre.
At least 56 people have died over the past eight days as the ATTF militants pursued a 17-year campaign for a separate tribal state.
Police said orders had been issued banning gatherings of more than five people in Agartala and neighbouring areas.

The separatists set ablaze at least 100 homes in the villages of Purbaramachandraghat and Ganda Basti and fired on fleeing residents, police in Agartala said. They then set fire to a third village, Gorangatilla.
It was the third attack in the Khowai area in a week. Tribal separatists set fire to more than 60 houses in ethnic clashes last Sunday and killed 17 people on Monday.

"Nobody who will indulge in violence will be spared," Chowdhury told Reuters on Sunday. "We are taking all steps to check violence, to ensure peace, so that life can fast return to normalcy. We have appealed to the people to maintain peace and harmony."
The ATTF issued a statement last July telling Bengali settlers to leave the state, which has an 840-km (520-mile) border with Bangladesh.
The state's indigenous tribal population has been reduced to a minority by Bengali Hindu immigrants who dominate local politics and the economy.
More than 2,000 people were killed in June 1980 in the region's worst ethnic riots.
